claims.text: UNHCR Flash Alert #21 reports that clashes in Baidoa between 3 and 5 September 2026 displaced more than 14,000 people.

UNHCR Flash Alert #24 (published Oct 2026) reports that renewed clashes in Baidoa, which began on 28 September 2026 and continued through 3 October 2026 between forces associated with the former Southwest State administration and the Somali National Army over control of the town, displaced 934 households (5,604 individuals) and caused 11 deaths and 86 injuries recorded at Bay Regional Hospital and Bayhaw Hospital, including eight deaths reportedly caused by stray bullets near RP Hotel; Southwest University, the RP Hotel, two mosques and three schools also reportedly sustained significant damage.

description: Clashes displaced civilians in Baidoa, Somalia, during 3–5 September and 28 September–3 October 2026. UNHCR reported more than 14,000 people displaced during the first period and an estimated 5,604 people (934 households) during the second; the reports do not establish a deduplicated total across both periods. The October alert described a fragile security situation, disrupted essential services, and urgent shelter, water, sanitation and protection needs.

impact.summary: UNHCR reported more than 14,000 people displaced during 3–5 September 2026 and an estimated 5,604 people (934 households) during 28 September–3 October; these separate reporting periods cannot be treated as a confirmed count of unique people. For the latter period, Flash Alert #24 reported 11 deaths and 86 injuries recorded at Bay Regional Hospital and Bayhaw Hospital, including eight deaths reportedly caused by stray bullets near RP Hotel. Southwest University, RP Hotel, two mosques and three schools reportedly sustained significant damage.

event.scale: Intermittent urban clashes for control of a regional capital

name: Baidoa Clashes & Displacement — South West State, Somalia

updates.text: Correction: the record begins with the 3–5 September clashes. More than 14,000 people were reported displaced then and an estimated 5,604 during 28 September–3 October; the previous combined figure of 19,600 is withdrawn because the reports do not establish a deduplicated total.

UNHCR's Flash Alert #24 document specifies that the 28 September-3 October round of clashes caused 11 deaths and 86 injuries (recorded at Bay Regional Hospital and Bayhaw Hospital), a casualty figure not previously quantified.
